exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Email Spoofing
exploitedBy.relevance: An open relay allows attackers to send spoofed emails through the misconfigured server without authentication.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Email Bombing
exploitedBy.relevance: Open relays are commonly abused to send large volumes of spam or bombing emails by relaying through the misconfigured server.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Guessing
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or missing SMTP authentication enables attackers to guess credentials to gain unauthorized access to the mail server.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Spraying
exploitedBy.relevance: Absent or weak SMTP authentication makes the service susceptible to password spraying attacks across multiple accounts.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak SMTP authentication allows credential stuffing attacks using previously breached username/password pairs.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Mail Protocols
exploitedBy.relevance: Cleartext SMTP transmission exposes mail protocol communications to interception and monitoring.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Email Collection
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted SMTP traffic allows attackers to collect email content and credentials through network interception.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Downgrade Attack
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak TLS cipher support enables downgrade attacks forcing connections to use weaker encryption protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Reduce Key Space
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak TLS ciphers reduce the effective key space, making encrypted communications easier to break.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Using outdated TLS protocol versions or weak ciphers directly weakens the encryption protecting email in transit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, attackers can flood the SMTP service with connections to cause a denial of service.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Brute Force
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient throttling allows unrestricted brute force attacks against mail server authentication.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
exploitedBy.relevance: An overprivileged MTA service account can be abused to escalate privileges or perform privileged actions on the host system.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Bypass User Account Control
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive privileges on the MTA service account may allow bypassing access controls to perform unauthorized system operations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched MTA software exposes known vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to compromise the public-facing mail server.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Known vulnerabilities in unpatched MTA software can be exploited remotely to gain unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Storing SMTP credentials in plaintext configuration files allows attackers to directly harvest them from the filesystem.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext credentials in config files represent unsecured credentials that can be easily extracted by adversaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Clear Mailbox Data
exploitedBy.relevance: Inadequate logging makes it difficult to detect or investigate mailbox data manipulation or deletion events.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Transport Agent
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient audit logging may fail to detect malicious transport agents installed on the mail server to intercept messages.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted management interface exposure allows attackers to remotely access and control the MTA using legitimate remote service protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of DANE leaves certificate validation reliant on CA trust, enabling attacks with fraudulent certificates during email transit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing DANE/MTA-STS policies that rely on DNS for enforcement can be undermined by DNS server compromise or manipulation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Embedded Payloads
exploitedBy.relevance: Disabled content filtering allows emails with embedded malicious payloads to reach end users undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: HTML Smuggling
exploitedBy.relevance: Without attachment and content filtering, HTML smuggling techniques in email attachments bypass security controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Fast Flux DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Without reverse DNS validation, fast flux DNS techniques can be used to obscure the true origin of malicious sending servers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Absent reverse lookup validation allows attackers to exploit DNS misconfigurations to misrepresent sending server identity.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Additional Email Delegate Permissions
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfigured mail queue directory permissions may allow unauthorized users to access or manipulate queued email data.
